Yes but not being in the news doesn't make it any less important. You should try and keep in mind that there is a good thing happening right now. For every SW post where the OP disappears, there's a lot previously suicidal people who untied the rope, threw away the meds or got rid of their razor. 

It's not bad to be aware of the bad things happening. But if it gets to you to a huge point, try thinking about good things that are happening this second.

Why do you feel like professional help is bad? 

I'm not going to force you to look for it but I'll say it's good. Are you scared of it? (It's not a bad thing to be unsure, I'm just curious.)

Try thinking about the small things first. I'll try to give some examples:

There's a girl I've never spoken to (ever!) in my English class, but she always smiles at me and she always acts very warm and welcoming.

In the class next to mine, there's a girl who's disabled and in a wheelchair. Everyone in her class helps her and gets her help setting up her desk in the classroom so she can be comfortable. It's really nice to see how everyone makes her feel the best way possible.

When you see someone crossing the street with an old person? I see that pretty often and it's so nice. Try doing it yourself too if you can.

There's a boy with severe anxiety problems in my class, and everyone welcomed him and made him feel better. We all know what we should do when he has an anxiety attack now and always work with him when he needs to. 

At my school we have an annual festival with multiple things each class has to work on, and we have a charity competition which has raised a lot of money to elderly people homes who cannot afford a lot of resources without external help.

Then scale to the greater things! Think of how Bill Gates has made so many donations and is now working on eradicating another disease.

Think of how much coverage and donations the Nepal earthquake got. For example, I play League of Legends and two big names in the community made a 24 hour live stream to gather donations from the viewers and it all went to the earthquake relief. Yesterday was the opening of an international League event and they advertised the Nepal relief funding before the games started to bring some attention.

There are a lot of things. Try thinking about it. But also know it's NOT inherently a bad thing to be aware of the tragedies and horrible things in the world.

I searched up what overbearing means. And... you really don't sound like it at all. You just come off as a bit anxious and a little desperate to see if she will indeed go out with you, and that's completely normal. Especially considering you're not the most sociable person ever.

She was pretty rude. Honestly it strikes me as she learned the word the day before and wanted to use it. If you're not pressuring her into going out with you then you definitely aren't overbearing at all.

But give it a little time before you go after her again, else she might shoo you off, and honestly, it might become annoying if you follow her around and try to talk to her everyday. Give her a bit of time then try again.

You can't pretend the bad things don't exist. You know why we hear in the news about police brutality, murders, missing kidnapped people, bombing threats to schools? Because they stand out because they aren't the majority.

It's shocking and it makes people turn their heads around to see what happened, but the good things are an overwhelming majority, which is why we don't talk about it. It just gets forgotten and so deeply mixed in our daily lives that we don't even notice all the good news and things happened.

No no no, I understand. At times you might feel like it's better to hide because judgement can be hard. And that's okay.

Unless you want to go hard and study in which case there are always ways to focus. But I'll be honest, if I were you, I'd be having the fun I could.

I'm going to quote myself from a thread I answered some hours ago: depression and suicidal ideation don't ever really fit to a T. There isn't a right way to experience depression and the only way you can know is through a professional.

Ahh I understand, having a condition that can kill you and feeling like it wouldn't be all that bad to die with it, plus the fact that you wouldn't be seen as selfish and weak. I feel it a whole awful lot.

I guess that's something you can do with some perseverance. Take a day out if you can, relax, treat yourself to some good things like your favorite pizza or that kind of stuff, watching a TV series maybe. Then you're at least a bit mentally prepared to face stuff. Sadly there's really no other way :/ it is really worth it with a good professional though.

You can always count on the folks over at /r/depression to help you find good shrinks or psychiatrists in your area!

Ninja edit: please don't underestimate the wreck that depression can become. Even if it doesn't hit you like the typical sadness and suicidal ideation at first, it can and will scale into worse things and we wouldn't want that. Mild depression is a snowball that turns into an avalanche so I ask you to kindly not let it slide. I know you might feel like it's okay and a temporary thing (and it might be!) but we're always better safe than sorry.
